Fixed-effect covariance and credible intervals for tobs_fit

Source: R/methods.R
tobs_fit_intervals.Rd

On a nested-Laplace fit that keeps the per-cell pieces of its outer grid (for example occu_cover() or abun() with an areal field), the covariance is the grid-marginalized one and the bounds invert the Gaussian mixture the grid defines, rather than being read off the Monte Carlo draws the fit also carries; coef(), summary() and tidy() read the same mixture. Every other fit reads as tulpa::vcov.tulpa_fit() / tulpa::confint.tulpa_fit() describe.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'tobs_fit'
vcov(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'tobs_fit'
confint(object, parm = NULL, level = 0.95, ...)

Arguments

object

A tobs_fit object.

...

Ignored.

parm

Parameter names or indices (default: all fixed effects). Indices address the fixed effects; a name that is not a fixed effect is read off the posterior draws when they carry a column of that name.

level

Interval level (default 0.95).

Value

vcov(): the fixed-effect covariance matrix. confint(): a two-column matrix of lower and upper bounds, one row per requested parameter, carrying the interval_source, interval_declined, retained_mass and skew_applied attributes tulpa::confint.tulpa_fit() documents.

Examples

# \donttest{
sim <- simulate_occu(N = 100, J = 3, n.occ.covs = 1, n.det.covs = 1,
                     seed = 1)
fit <- tobs(~ occ_cov1, data = sim$data, family = occu(),
            detection = ~ det_cov1, y = sim$y, method = "laplace",
            control = list(verbose = FALSE, progress = FALSE))
vcov(fit)
confint(fit, level = 0.9)
# }
